kor_events.0.d.before:
In 1906, after the Korean-Japanese-Russian War had left the entire peninsula in ruins, the Republic of Korea was born on the corpse of the old empire: the first democratic republic in Korean history, and in Asia. For the past thirty years, it has continued to develop.

As we walked a precarious tightrope between the great powers, modernisation and economic growth greatly improved our people's lives. When the Great War broke out in Europe, we remained neutral. While white men spilled one another's blood, we made money selling them supplies and sending them workers. Most of the unequal treaties were revised, and the first chaebol business conglomerates and an embryonic capitalist economy emerged. Economic growth, modernisation and democracy also nourished vigorous movements for civil rights, women's rights and the abolition of oppressive feudal customs.

The Great Depression changed everything. The Seoul Stock Exchange was forced to close early, countless companies and factories went bankrupt, and many citizens found themselves suddenly unemployed. All the republic's prosperity vanished like a mirage.

Amid the mounting social turmoil, a non-violent civil disobedience movement erupted on 18 May 1931 in Daegu, a city known for its strong socialist sympathies as "Joseon's Moscow". The demonstrators demanded food, jobs, doctors and Syngman Rhee's resignation. Rhee's government sent tanks to crush these 200,000 "reds" demanding the president's departure, sparing neither men nor women, young nor old.

After the bloody suppression of the Daegu Socialisation Movement, Lyuh Woon-hyung's Korean Social Democratic Party and Pak Hon-yong's Workers' Party of Joseon were blamed for organising the protests and forcibly dissolved. Democracy has withered and public life has grown increasingly repressive. Democrats have rallied under the Liberal–Independence Party Coalition to defend democracy, but containing extremist political forces now seems beyond them.

Meanwhile, Japan has invaded Manchuria through its leased territory at Dalian and established a puppet state there. Invoking Hakko Ichiu, the ideal of bringing the world under one roof, and the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, it makes no secret of its desire to avenge the Korean-Japanese-Russian War and conquer us. Yet the League of Nations does nothing. The Europeans are preoccupied with their own problems, the Chinese are busy fighting one another, and the Americans continue their isolationist course. No one seems likely to help us.

Will the Republic of Korea still be independent ten years from now?

kor_events.70.d.before: The day has finally come for the presidential election held every five years since Philip Jaisohn founded the Republic of Korea in 1906. No president has yet served four consecutive terms. Citing the unstable world situation and recent events, President Syngman Rhee has nevertheless broken with tradition once again and insisted on running for a fourth term. His challenger is Ahn Chang-ho of the Independence Party. Formerly a Liberal, Ahn publicly denounced the incumbent as 'a damned dictator blinded by power' over his fourth-term bid, the bloody suppression of the Daegu Socialisation Movement in 1931 and his pro-chaebol policies. He then left the Liberals, joined the Independence Party and became its presidential candidate.\n\nWe can choose whether the Liberal Party wins or the Independence Party brings a change of government.

He then left the Liberals, joined the Independence Party and became its presidential candidate.\n\nWe can choose whether the Liberal Party wins or the Independence Party brings a change of government.

KOR_agitate_the_union_desc.before: Under the security crackdown that followed the Great Depression, the freedom to form trade unions guaranteed by Article 33 of the Republic's constitution has become a dead letter. Unions are collapsing one after another under repression by the police and hired thugs employed by the chaebol business conglomerates. We must give them weapons and invite them to join our cause.
KOR_agitate_the_union_desc.after: Under the security crackdown that followed the Great Depression, the freedom to form trade unions guaranteed by Article 33 of the Republic's constitution has become a dead letter. Unions are collapsing one after another under repression by the police and hired thugs employed by the corporate oligarchs. We must give them weapons and invite them to join our cause.

KOR_confiscation_of_chaebol_assets_desc.before: The chaebol have amassed their fortunes by sucking the blood of workers and peasants. Even the Great Depression did nothing to curb their insatiable greed. Their property will now be confiscated by the workers' and peasants' republic, and every last part of their accumulated wealth will be redistributed.
KOR_confiscation_of_chaebol_assets_desc.after: The corporate oligarchs have amassed their fortunes by sucking the blood of workers and peasants. Even the Great Depression did nothing to curb their insatiable greed. Their property will now be confiscated by the workers' and peasants' republic, and every last part of their accumulated wealth will be redistributed.

KOR_purge_reactionarist_desc.before: During the Korean Revolutionary War, we arrested great numbers of Liberal-Independence Party politicians, collaborators in Syngman Rhee's army, police officers, landowners and chaebol magnates, together with every member of their families. They are enemies of the revolution, subversives with no place in the new workers' and peasants' republic. Fair trials before the people's courts will establish their guilt or innocence and deliver 'appropriate' punishment...
KOR_purge_reactionarist_desc.after: During the Korean Revolutionary War, we arrested great numbers of Liberal-Independence Party politicians, collaborators in Syngman Rhee's army, police officers, landowners and corporate oligarchs, together with every member of their families. They are enemies of the revolution, subversives with no place in the new workers' and peasants' republic. Fair trials before the people's courts will establish their guilt or innocence and deliver 'appropriate' punishment...

KOR_cooperation_with_the_jaebeol_desc.before: Although the Great Depression bankrupted most businesses and factories, some chaebol business conglomerates managed to weather its effects. We should grant them modest privileges, encouraging them to put their capabilities to work for our country.
KOR_cooperation_with_the_jaebeol_desc.after: Although the Great Depression bankrupted most businesses and factories, some conglomerates controlled by the corporate oligarchs managed to weather its effects. We should grant them modest privileges, encouraging them to put their capabilities to work for our country.

KOR_taming_the_jaebeol_desc.before: The chaebol have long clung to civilian politicians, enriching themselves by exploiting ordinary decent people through collusion between business and politics. During the coup, however, we seized all their Seoul headquarters, and their chairmen are now detained in Intelligence Command safe houses. We will summon them all and demand loyalty to the military regime. They can come aboard with us, or go to Samcheong Re-education Camp.
KOR_taming_the_jaebeol_desc.after: The corporate oligarchs have long clung to civilian politicians, enriching themselves by exploiting ordinary decent people through collusion between business and politics. During the coup, however, we seized all the Seoul headquarters of their conglomerates, and the chairmen are now detained in Intelligence Command safe houses. We will summon them all and demand loyalty to the military regime. They can come aboard with us, or go to Samcheong Re-education Camp.

KOR_great_depression_desc.before: Beginning with the American stock market crash of 1929, the Great Depression has spread across the world and dealt a severe blow to the Korean economy. Unemployment has soared and tax revenues have plummeted. Almost every business except a handful of chaebol conglomerates and their affiliates has gone bankrupt. Even now, our streets are filled with long queues of unemployed people at soup kitchens and the sight of gaunt women and children begging.
KOR_great_depression_desc.after: Beginning with the American stock market crash of 1929, the Great Depression has spread across the world and dealt a severe blow to the Korean economy. Unemployment has soared and tax revenues have plummeted. Almost every business except a handful of family-controlled conglomerates and their affiliates has gone bankrupt. Even now, our streets are filled with long queues of unemployed people at soup kitchens and the sight of gaunt women and children begging.

KOR_jaebeol_category_desc.before: Chaebol are family-controlled business conglomerates whose senior management is drawn from the same extended family. They wield enormous influence over this country's economy. By granting them favourable treatment, we can secure their help in developing it.
KOR_jaebeol_category_desc.after: The corporate oligarchs control family-owned business conglomerates whose senior management is drawn from the same extended family. They wield enormous influence over this country's economy. By granting them favourable treatment, we can secure their help in developing it.
